"""Runs 6 (e-side n=+3.2e12) and 7 (h-side n=-1.2e12): raw R(B), 1/B FFT, per-tone onsets.
Grounds the landau-fan design (B_lo, B_hi, tone structure vs F_L)."""
import numpy as np, json, warnings
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, resolve_channels, sdh_fft, sdh_onset, SdhOnsetError, luttinger_frequency

CAL = json.load(open("hera_scratch/cal_run5.json"))
out = {}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(13, 11))
for j, (rid, n12) in enumerate([(6, 3.2), (7, -1.2)]):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}")
    ch = {c.cid: c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    B = r.col("magnet_field"); I = r.col("sr0_X") / ch["sr0"].gain
    R = (r.col("sr1_X") / ch["sr1"].gain) / I
    T = r.col("T_sample")
    o = np.argsort(B); B, R, I, T = B[o], R[o], I[o], T[o]
    FL = luttinger_frequency(abs(n12) * 1e16)
    print(f"\n=== run {rid}: n = {n12:+.2f}e12, F_L(full, 4-fold) = {FL:.2f} T; T {T.min():.3f}-{T.max():.3f} K; "
          f"I {I.min()*1e9:.2f}-{I.max()*1e9:.2f} nA; R {R.min():.1f}..{R.max():.1f} Ohm, R(B~0) = {R[B<0.1].mean():.1f}")
    # signed R minima (near-zero / negative -> QH-like minima)
    ax[0, j].plot(B, R, lw=0.8); ax[0, j].set_title(f"run {rid}: n = {n12:+.2f}e12, D = 0 — raw Rxx(B)"); ax[0, j].set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax[0, j].set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)")
    ax[0, j].axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.5)
    # FFT windows
    for lo, hi, col in [(1.5, 10.0, "C0"), (3.0, 10.0, "C1"), (1.5, 5.0, "C2")]:
        m = (B >= lo) & (B <= hi)
        f, sp = sdh_fft(R[m][:, None], B[m], nfft=2048, bg_degree=5, log=False)
        sp = sp[0]
        sel = (f > 1) & (f < 150)
        ax[1, j].plot(f[sel], sp[sel] / sp[sel].max(), color=col, lw=0.9, label=f"B {lo}-{hi} T")
        pk = f[sel][np.argsort(sp[sel])[::-1][:6]]
        print(f"  FFT window {lo}-{hi} T top freqs: {np.round(np.sort(pk),1)} T")
    for k in (1, 2, 4):
        ax[1, j].axvline(FL / k, color="gray", ls=":", lw=0.8)
    ax[1, j].set_xlim(0, 80); ax[1, j].set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax[1, j].set_ylabel("|FFT| (norm)"); ax[1, j].legend(fontsize=7)
    ax[1, j].set_title(f"1/B FFT (dotted: F_L, F_L/2, F_L/4 = {FL:.1f}/{FL/2:.1f}/{FL/4:.1f} T)")
    # onset
    try:
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            on = sdh_onset(R, B, b_lo=0.3, r_full_scale=50e-6 / 10e-9)
        print(on.summary())
        out[rid] = dict(onset_b=float(on.onset_b), tones=[(float(t.freq), float(t.contrast), float(t.onset_b), t.harmonic_of) for t in on.tones])
    except SdhOnsetError as e:
        print("  sdh_onset failed:", e)
    # 1/B view w/ background removed
    m = B >= 1.0
    cf = np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5); dR = R[m] - np.polyval(cf, B[m])
    ax[2, j].plot(1 / B[m], dR, lw=0.7); ax[2, j].set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax[2, j].set_ylabel("dRxx (Ohm), poly5 removed"); ax[2, j].set_title("oscillatory part vs 1/B (B >= 1 T)")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/sdh_spot_runs6_7.png", dpi=110)
json.dump(out, open("hera_scratch/sdh_spot_onsets.json", "w"), indent=1, default=str)
print("saved hera_scratch/sdh_spot_runs6_7.png")

Appends markdown and/or code cells at the end of a JupyterLab-open notebook

filtered and timed later. Re-running with the same args double-inserts.

positional arguments:

                        all --markdown/--code variants.
  --markdown-file PATH  Append a markdown cell whose source is read from PATH
                        (UTF-8). Repeatable; order-preserved.
  --code-file PATH      Append an un-executed code cell whose source is read
                        from PATH (UTF-8). Repeatable; order-preserved.
  --summary TEXT        One-line dense spec of the proposed measurement.

                        cell. Requires at least one markdown cell among the

entries.name: CronCreate
entries.description:
Schedule a prompt to be enqueued at a future time. Use for both recurring schedules and one-shot reminders.

Uses standard 5-field cron in the user's local timezone: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. "0 9 * * *" means 9am local — no timezone conversion needed.

## One-shot tasks (recurring: false)

For "remind me at X" or "at <time>, do Y" requests — fire once then auto-delete.
Pin minute/hour/day-of-month/month to specific values:
  "remind me at 2:30pm today to check the deploy" → cron: "30 14 <today_dom> <today_month> *", recurring: false
  "tomorrow morning, run the smoke test" → cron: "57 8 <tomorrow_dom> <tomorrow_month> *", recurring: false

## Recurring jobs (recurring: true, the default)

For "every N minutes" / "every hour" / "weekdays at 9am" requests:
  "*/5 * * * *" (every 5 min), "0 * * * *" (hourly), "0 9 * * 1-5" (weekdays at 9am local)

## Avoid the :00 and :30 minute marks when the task allows it

Every user who asks for "9am" gets `0 9`, and every user who asks for "hourly" gets `0 *` — which means requests from across the planet land on the API at the same instant. When the user's request is approximate, pick a minute that is NOT 0 or 30:
  "every morning around 9" → "57 8 * * *" or "3 9 * * *" (not "0 9 * * *")
  "hourly" → "7 * * * *" (not "0 * * * *")
  "in an hour or so, remind me to..." → pick whatever minute you land on, don't round

Only use minute 0 or 30 when the user names that exact time and clearly means it ("at 9:00 sharp", "at half past", coordinating with a meeting). When in doubt, nudge a few minutes early or late — the user will not notice, and the fleet will.

## Session-only

Jobs live only in this Claude session — nothing is written to disk, and the job is gone when Claude exits.

## Not for live watching

CronCreate re-runs a prompt at fixed wall-clock intervals. To watch a log file, process, or command output and be notified the moment something changes, use the Monitor tool instead — Monitor streams events as they happen; cron polls on a schedule.

## Runtime behavior

Jobs only fire while the REPL is idle (not mid-query). The scheduler adds a small deterministic jitter on top of whatever you pick: recurring tasks fire up to 10% of their period late (max 15 min); one-shot tasks landing on :00 or :30 fire up to 90 s early. Picking an off-minute is still the bigger lever.

Recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days — they fire one final time, then are deleted. This bounds session lifetime. Tell the user about the 7-day limit when scheduling recurring jobs.

Returns a job ID you can pass to CronDelete.

cron.description: Standard 5-field cron expression in local time: "M H DoM Mon DoW" (e.g. "*/5 * * * *" = every 5 minutes, "30 14 28 2 *" = Feb 28 at 2:30pm local once).

prompt.description: The prompt to enqueue at each fire time.

recurring.description: true (default) = fire on every cron match until deleted or auto-expired after 7 days. false = fire once at the next match, then auto-delete. Use false for "remind me at X" one-shot requests with pinned minute/hour/dom/month.

durable.description: Has no effect — durable persistence is not available. All jobs are session-only (in-memory, gone when this Claude session ends).

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 10 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 600000ms are capped to 600000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

Goal: ABAB / ABCA / ABCB / cannot-tell for the one measured pair (sr1 = B_1−B_2), evidence-cited.
Discriminator: the Landau-level structure in a (n, B) fan at D = 0 — (a) the zero-energy LL degeneracy
(first gaps from the CNP: ν = ±8 bilayer-like, ±16 ABCA / two-bilayer ABAB, mixed set for ABCB),
(b) the number of Fermi pockets at finite n (ABAB: two bilayer-like pockets → two line families with
distinct per-pocket ν; ABCA: one family; ABCB: a light Dirac-like pocket + a heavy one), (c) how the
gaps evolve with D (fan 2).

## Done (previous instance)
1. Gate C runs 0–3: alive on the provided pair, no leakage (pA floor), Rxx 60–330 Ω at B = 0.
2. Gatemap run 5 (run 4 aborted, railed): two parallel CNP ridges (region A dominant, region B
   electron-doped by 0.43e12 — series mosaic confound). Calibration (cal_run5.json): c_bg/c_tg = 0.773
   (data), c_tg = 2.796 mF/m² (9.5 nm prior — absolute n scale still a prior), n_offset −0.089e12,
   D_offset −0.013 V/nm from R_CNP(D) symmetry. D = 0 line inside validators: n = −1.27 … +3.27e12.
3. SdH spot checks at D = 0: run 6 (n = +3.2e12, 0→10 T, 10 mT), run 7 (n = −1.2e12, 10→0.3 T, 20 mT).
   My read (hera_scratch/sdh_spot_runs6_7.png): run 6 has QH minima to Rxx ≈ 0 at ~2.3, 3.4, 4.2, 6.0,
   7.2 T and a 530 Ω hump 8–10 T; tones 7.1 T (dominant, onset < 0.3 T) + 14.1 / 22.1 / 29.5–30 T.
   Either ABAB two pockets (model 7.5 / 25.6 T — observed 7.1 / ~30, sum 37 vs F_L 33: a ~10 % n-scale
   error would fit) or one pocket F_L ≈ 30 T with F_L/2, F_L/4 subharmonics (every 4th gap deep).
   Run 7: tones 12.3 T (≈ F_L 12.4, SNR 124), 6.6, 4.7, 8.5, 9.4; minima at ~2.0, 3.4, 4.6, 5.8, 7.3 T.
   Spot checks cannot separate "two pockets" from "one pocket + subharmonics" — the fan can.

## Next
4. **landau-fan #1, D = 0 (this step).** Fast: (Vtg, Vbg) co-swept along the calibrated D = 0 line,
   n = −1.25 … +3.25e12, 151 pts (0.03e12; TG −0.291 … +0.998 V, BG −0.484 … +1.185 V). Slow: B
   1.0 → 3.8 T at 0.2 T (15 rows) then 4.0 → 10.0 T at 0.1 T (61 rows); 76 rows, 11 476 pts. Uniform
   in B because LL lines are straight in (n, B); coarse below 4 T where ν lines are dense anyway
   (ν = 4 spacing = 4 fast steps at 1 T), fine above where the ν assignment is made (ν = 1 → 8 steps at
   10 T; window covers ν −5 … +13 at 10 T, −10 … +27 at 5 T). sr1 fixed 200 µV = 20 kΩ FS (a rail only
   at ν = 0 at high B, not diagnostic). fast_delay 1.0 s (≈ 1.0 s/pt measured, run 5), slow_delay 3 s.
   Price 4.6 h (+10 % → ~5.1 h), ends at 10 T with gates parked at 0.
   Establishes: LL line intercepts (region A vs B CNPs), ν sequence on both sides, pocket count.
   Checkpoints: first 2 rows (signal, no rail, gate current pA, T); ~every 1–1.5 h re-form partial fan
   (fan_grids) — abandon if featureless or railing across the window.
5. **Land runs 6/7 + fan analysis in ana** (raw → FFT/onset → take), while the fan runs.
6. **Fan #2 riding 10 → 1 T** — choice depends on fan #1: finite D (D ≈ +0.15–0.25 V/nm, where the
   gatemap ridge is gapped: gap-vs-D and LL crossings separate ABAB from ABCB) or, if fan #1 is
   ambiguous on the hole side, a denser hole-side fan. Never re-traverse: fan 2 descends.
7. **Call** in ana (output contract), then `return-to-initial` close-out on operator ask.

## What would change my mind
- Fan #1 shows two line families with different slopes converging on one CNP → two pockets (ABAB-like);
  one family with alternating gap depth → subharmonics (ABCA-like); a ν = ±2/±4 Dirac-like family on top
  of a heavy family → ABCB candidate.
- If the first gap from the CNP at 10 T is at |ν| = 8 on both sides, ABAB (two bilayer-like zero modes
  split by interlayer coupling) vs ABCA (16-fold) is settled by the ν = ±12 presence/absence.
- Region B (n offset +0.43e12) will add a second intercept; lines not extrapolating to n = 0 are B's.
- T_e ≈ 8 K on this rig: absence of odd/symmetry-broken ν is not evidence.

from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

# --- session calibration from run 5 (cnp-and-dline-calibration; ratio data-calibrated, scale = geometry prior) ---
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
n_line = np.linspace(-1.25, 3.25, 151)          # 1e12 cm^-2, 0.03e12 step, hole -> electron
D_line = 0.0                                    # V/nm
Vtg_line, Vbg_line = calc_gate_voltages(n_line, np.full_like(n_line, D_line), CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
assert Vtg_line.min() >= TG_MIN and Vtg_line.max() <= TG_MAX, (Vtg_line.min(), Vtg_line.max())
assert Vbg_line.min() >= BG_MIN and Vbg_line.max() <= BG_MAX, (Vbg_line.min(), Vbg_line.max())
print(f"fast line: n {n_line[0]:+.2f} -> {n_line[-1]:+.2f}e12 ({len(n_line)} pts, {n_line[1]-n_line[0]:.3f}e12), D = {D_line:+.2f} V/nm; "
      f"Vtg {Vtg_line.min():+.4f}..{Vtg_line.max():+.4f} V, Vbg {Vbg_line.min():+.4f}..{Vbg_line.max():+.4f} V (limits TG [{TG_MIN},{TG_MAX}], BG [{BG_MIN},{BG_MAX}])")

# --- field grid: uniform in B (LL lines straight in (n, B)); coarse below 4 T, fine above where nu is assigned
B_vec = np.round(np.concatenate((np.arange(1.0, 3.8001, 0.2), np.arange(4.0, 10.0001, 0.1))), 3)
assert B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP and np.all(np.diff(B_vec) > 0)
print(f"slow B: {len(B_vec)} rows, {B_vec[0]} -> {B_vec[-1]} T (0.2 T to 3.8, 0.1 T from 4.0); {len(B_vec)*len(n_line)} pts")

# --- preconditions (assumed, not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0 = T_sample(), magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B|<0.05: handoff left 0 T), V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), "
      f"nplci tg/bg = {k_tg.nplci()}/{k_bg.nplci()} (1/1), PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.05 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert k_tg.nplci() == 1 and k_bg.nplci() == 1, "gate-current nplci not 1"
assert magnet.persistent_switch_on() and magnet.output_enabled()

FAST_DELAY, SLOW_DELAY = 1.0, 3.0
I_TRIP = 1e-9
# Fixed sensitivity for the whole fan: 200 uV = 20 kOhm FS at 10 nA. Run 6/7 maxima <= 590 Ohm at 10 T away from the CNP;
# only the nu = 0 region at high B can exceed 20 kOhm (a rail there is not diagnostic). Quantization ~0.3 Ohm.
sr1.sensitivity(200e-6)

mc = dict(meas_config); mc["Si (V)"] = k_si(); mc["sample_temperature:"] = _T0
mc["comments"] = (f"landau-fan D = {D_line:+.2f} V/nm (run-5 cal): fast (Vtg,Vbg) along n = {n_line[0]:+.2f}..{n_line[-1]:+.2f}e12 ({len(n_line)} pts), "
                  f"slow B {B_vec[0]}..{B_vec[-1]} T ({len(B_vec)} rows: 0.2 T to 3.8, 0.1 T from 4.0), sr1 200 uV, fast_delay 1 s")
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('landau-fan')
s.add_comment(f'D = {D_line:+.2f} V/nm; fast n = {n_line[0]:+.2f} -> {n_line[-1]:+.2f}e12 cm^-2 ({len(n_line)} pts, {n_line[1]-n_line[0]:.3f}e12) as co-swept (Vtg, Vbg); '
              f'slow B = {B_vec[0]} -> {B_vec[-1]} T ({len(B_vec)} rows); cal run 5: ratio {CAL["c_bg"]/CAL["c_tg"]:.3f}, c_tg {CAL["c_tg"]:.3e} (prior), '
              f'n_offset {CAL["n_offset"]:+.3f}e12, D_offset {CAL["D_offset"]:+.3f}; Vsi = 0; T_sample {_T0:.3f} K')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbg_line[0]); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtg_line[0])
interruptible_sleep(10)

# row layout: [time, B, Vtg, Vbg, T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.X); s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.P); s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr0.X)
s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr); s.plot('time', T_sample)

def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[5])), abs(float(data[6]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        print(f"LEAK TRIP at B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T, Vtg={float(data[2]):+.3f}, Vbg={float(data[3]):+.3f}: |I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A")
        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

try:
    s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtg_line, Vbg_line],
                     slow_delay=SLOW_DELAY, fast_delay=FAST_DELAY)
finally:
    # gates parked at 0; field stays where the fan ends (10 T) — fan #2 rides it down, never re-traverse.
    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)
print(f"done: B = {magnet.field():+.3f} T, (Vtg, Vbg) = ({k_tg.volt():+.4f}, {k_bg.volt():+.4f}), T_sample = {T_sample():.3f} K")

## HERA — Step 4: Landau fan #1 at D = 0 (`landau-fan`), n = −1.25 … +3.25×10¹² × B 1 → 10 T

**Why this, now (plan step 4; operator ask: the fan for the stacking call).** The spot checks (runs 6, 7 — my read in ana, next cell) show well-developed quantum oscillations at D = 0: run 6 (n = +3.2×10¹²) has Rxx minima to ≈ 0 Ω at ~2.3, 3.4, 4.2, 6.0, 7.2 T with tones 7.1 T (dominant) + 14.1 / 22.1 / ~30 T; run 7 (n = −1.2×10¹²) tones 12.3 T (≈ F_L = 12.4) + 6.6 / 4.7 / 8.5 T. The electron-side pair 7.1 / ~30 T is *either* two pockets (ABAB-like light + heavy bilayer bands: model 7.5 / 25.6 T) *or* one pocket at F_L ≈ 30 T with F_L/2, F_L/4 subharmonics (every 4th gap deep, ABCA-like). A 1D trace cannot tell those apart; a fan can — two pockets give two line families with different slopes through one CNP, subharmonics give one family with alternating gap depth — and it reads the zero-LL degeneracy directly (first gap at |ν| = 8 vs 16 from the CNP). Run 5's region-B mosaic (CNP offset +0.43×10¹²) will show up as a second intercept, so the fan also separates the two regions' lines.

**Design.** Fast axis: (V_tg, V_bg) co-swept along the calibrated D = 0 line (run-5 cal: ratio 0.773, c_tg prior, n_offset −0.089, D_offset −0.013), n = −1.25 → +3.25×10¹² in 151 points (0.030×10¹²; TG −0.291 … +0.998 V, BG −0.484 … +1.185 V — 2 mV inside the TG limit on the electron end, hole end TG-limited at −0.29 V). Coverage trade: the hole side reaches only n = −1.25 (TG −0.3 V limit) — at 10 T that is ν = −5, at 4 T ν = −13, so the hole-side zero-LL degeneracy is read at B ≲ 6.5 T (ν = −8) rather than 10 T; the electron side reaches ν = +13 at 10 T, +27 at 5 T. Slow axis uniform in B (LL lines are straight in (n, B)): 1.0 → 3.8 T at 0.2 T (15 rows — lines dense there, ν = 4 spacing ≈ 4 fast steps at 1 T), 4.0 → 10.0 T at 0.1 T (61 rows — ν = 1 spacing = 8 fast steps at 10 T). 76 rows × 151 = 11 476 pts. Sensitivity fixed at 200 µV (20 kΩ FS at 10 nA): runs 6/7 peaked at 590 Ω; only ν = 0 at high B can rail, and that is not diagnostic. fast_delay 1.0 s (τ = 0.3 s / 24 dB, a uniform ~1-step lag in n, slopes untouched — same as run 5), slow_delay 3 s; leak guard > 1 nA either gate → interrupt. Ends at **10 T with gates parked at 0 V** (fan #2 rides the magnet down — never re-traverse).

**Price** (from run 5: 1.0 s/pt + ~8 s row turnaround; magnet 0.137 T/min + 3 s settle): 0 → 1 T ramp 7 min; 15 coarse rows × 250 s + 61 fine rows × 206 s ≈ 4.6 h → **~5.1 h realistic (+10 %)**. **Checkpoints:** first 2 rows (signal on sr1, no rail, gate currents at the pA floor, T_sample ≈ 1.2 K, field tracking) via `hera-watch`; then ~every 1–1.5 h a re-formed partial fan (`fan_grids`) — abandon if featureless or railing across the window (price of a continue call: the remaining rows).

"""Runs 6 (e-side, n = +3.2e12) and 7 (h-side, n = -1.2e12) — sdh-spot-check at D = 0. Raw Rxx(B) first, then the
1/B FFT (three windows) and per-tone onsets (sdh_onset); F_L = |n| h / 4e from the run-5 calibration for reference."""
import warnings
from hera.analysis import resolve_channels, sdh_onset, SdhOnsetError

spots = [(6, 3.2), (7, -1.2)]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(13, 11))
for j, (rid, n12) in enumerate(spots):
    r = run(rid)
    ch = {c.cid: c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    B = r.col("magnet_field"); I = r.col("sr0_X") / ch["sr0"].gain
    R = (r.col("sr1_X") / ch["sr1"].gain) / I; T = r.col("T_sample")
    o = np.argsort(B); B, R, I, T = B[o], R[o], I[o], T[o]
    FL = luttinger_frequency(abs(n12) * 1e16)
    print(f"=== run {rid}: n = {n12:+.2f}e12 (run-5 cal), D = 0; F_L(4-fold, full n) = {FL:.2f} T; T {T.min():.3f}-{T.max():.3f} K; "
          f"I_drain {I.min()*1e9:.2f}-{I.max()*1e9:.2f} nA; Rxx {R.min():.0f}..{R.max():.0f} Ohm; complete={r.complete}")
    # raw
    ax[0, j].plot(B, R, lw=0.8); ax[0, j].axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.5)
    ax[0, j].set_title(f"run {rid}: n = {n12:+.2f}e12, D = 0 — raw Rxx(B), sr1 = B_1-B_2"); ax[0, j].set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax[0, j].set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)")
    # FFT in 1/B, three windows
    for lo, hi, col in [(1.5, 10.0, "C0"), (3.0, 10.0, "C1"), (1.5, 5.0, "C2")]:
        m = (B >= lo) & (B <= hi)
        f, sp = sdh_fft(R[m][:, None], B[m], nfft=2048, bg_degree=5, log=False); sp = sp[0]
        sel = (f > 1) & (f < 150)
        ax[1, j].plot(f[sel], sp[sel] / sp[sel].max(), color=col, lw=0.9, label=f"B {lo}-{hi} T")
        pk = np.sort(f[sel][np.argsort(sp[sel])[::-1][:6]])
        print(f"  FFT {lo}-{hi} T, top-6 freqs: {np.round(pk, 1)} T")
    for k in (1, 2, 4): ax[1, j].axvline(FL / k, color="gray", ls=":", lw=0.8)
    ax[1, j].set_xlim(0, 80); ax[1, j].set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax[1, j].set_ylabel("|FFT| (norm)"); ax[1, j].legend(fontsize=7)
    ax[1, j].set_title(f"1/B FFT — dotted F_L, F_L/2, F_L/4 = {FL:.1f} / {FL/2:.1f} / {FL/4:.1f} T")

**Read.** *Run 6 (electron, n = +3.2×10¹²):* quantum oscillations from < 1 T, with Rxx minima reaching ≈ 0 Ω at ~2.3, 3.4, 4.2, 6.0 and 7.2 T (quantum-Hall minima, i.e. the device is clean enough for a fan), then a 530 Ω hump 8–10 T. Tones: **7.1 T dominant** (visible to the low edge of the record, harmonics at 14.1 / 22.1 / 29.5 T flagged), plus a **~30 T** component that owns the 3–10 T window. F_L(4-fold, full n) = 33.1 T. Two readings fit: (i) two pockets — light 7.1 T + heavy ~30 T, sum 37 T ≈ F_L within the ~10 % n-scale prior (the ABAB-like light/heavy bilayer-band pair); (ii) one pocket F_L ≈ 30 T with F_L/2 and F_L/4 subharmonics — every 4th gap deep (ABCA-like 16-fold pattern). A 1D trace cannot separate these. *Run 7 (hole, n = −1.2×10¹²):* minima at ~2.0 (≈ 0 Ω), 3.4, 4.6, 5.8, 7.3 T; tones 12.3 T (≈ F_L = 12.4, SNR 124), 6.6 (≈ F_L/2), 4.7, 8.5, 9.4 T — same ambiguity (F_L + F_L/2 vs a 4.7/6.6–8.5 pair).
